Marissa / Rishi — thanks. I'm elevating to Exec Ops: Lydia, first apology for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev2 and will provide 15-min cadence updates until restored.

Summary so far (prelim):
- Timeline: last night's automated tiering job reassigned several MedixHealth projects to the "standard-tier" for cost alignment; appears a label mismatch caused a subset of critical projects to be mapped to an org-level quota that is much lower than expected.
- Impact: surge of 429s and client retry storms as Medix's production traffic hit the unexpected quota ceiling.

Immediate mitigation plan (now):
1) Rishi to confirm live quota mappings and pin Medix projects back to their prior tier (manual override) — target 30 mins.
2) Apply emergency per-project override (temporary increase) while we validate the mapping fix.
3) Enable a localized rate-smoothing proxy to drop client retries and avoid downstream amplification (if needed).
4) Post-mortem: roll back the last tiering run, add validation, and create a canary check for future jobs.

Naomi — please prepare an exec note for Medix leadership summarizing impact and remedies; include a credit proposal (we can discuss offline).

Rishi — priority to you. Keep the thread updated with precise ETA. I'll join the bridge in 10.

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability

> Hi Luke — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I'm looping in our on-call infra (Rishi) and Jonas so we can escalate.

Update (post-triage):
- Root cause: automated tiering job erroneously matched project labels when multiple projects shared the same short label (label collision). As a result ~6 critical Medix project IDs were mapped to a lower org quota bucket.
- Action taken (12:40 PDT): manually pinned affected projects back to their previous high-throughput tier and applied a 10x emergency per-project override.
- Immediate effect: 429s fell from ~42% -> ~4% within 6 minutes; overall p95 latency returned to <200ms. We've also rate-limited aggressive client retries for 30 minutes to prevent re-amplification.
- Next steps:
  * Re-run tiering with safe-mode (dry-run + strict label disambiguation) and a canary subset.
  * Deploy a validation job to assert post-cutover quotas for top-100 accounts.
  * Share a draft post-mortem and reparation proposal to Medix (including one month of service credit and a timeline for automation fixes).

Attachments: runbook-ratecap-fix-v1.md

I'll follow up with logs and the short-term graphs to include in the customer update.

-Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
